As I sit here, staring out the window at the rain-soaked streets of London, I find myself grappling with a profound sense of disquiet. I remember the days when I used to dream of a future where technology would liberate us from the drudgery of manual labour, where we could pursue our passions without the burden of toil. I remember the days when I believed that the march of progress would inevitably lead us to a utopian future, where we would transcend the limitations of our biological bodies and become something more than mere biological machines.

The very technologies that were supposed to liberate us have instead become instruments of control, tools for the surveillance and manipulation of the masses.
